This site summarizes the BFD fungal genome database across the main functional areas. Every figure uses **one representative genome per species** (best BUSCO complete, then N50; annotated genomes only). Each figure is shown at four taxonomic levels, as tabs: **Phylum**, **Subphylum** (derived from the class, because the database's subphylum column is empty; classes without a known subphylum keep their phylum label, see Data and methods), **Class** and **Order**. Groups are ordered and coloured by their parent phylum, so related classes sit together. Group values are medians or means **over genomes**, never over proteins, so large genomes do not dominate. At phylum level the eight largest phyla are shown and the rest pooled; at subphylum and class level groups with fewer than 10 genomes are pooled as "Other (small groups)".

These pages describe the database; they do not test hypotheses. For tested hypotheses with effect sizes and caveats see the [summary atlas](https://github.com/stajichlab/BFD_dashboard/blob/main/docs/summary_atlas/index.md) and [FUNCTIONAL_ANALYSES](https://github.com/stajichlab/BFD_dashboard/blob/main/docs/FUNCTIONAL_ANALYSES.md).

## Genomes per group

```{python}
fig("F01_genomes_by_group", "Representative genomes per group.")
table("T00_group_key")
```

### What is in the grey "Other" group

The grey group pools every taxon that is too small to show on its own (outside the top eight phyla at phylum level, fewer than 10 genomes at subphylum and class level). It is a mixture of unrelated taxa, so read it as "everything else", not as a lineage. The table lists exactly which taxa it contains.

```{python}
table("T00b_other_members", max_rows=40)
```
